card.title: Translational equilibrium
card.body: $\sum \vec{F} = \vec{0}$, which in two dimensions means **both** $\sum F_x = 0$ and $\sum F_y = 0$ (so $\vec{a} = \vec{0}$).
card.says: equilibrium covers **both** staying at rest (static equilibrium, $\vec{v} = \vec{0}$) and moving at constant velocity (dynamic equilibrium, $\vec{v} = \text{const} \ne \vec{0}$).
card.from: Newton's first law resolved into perpendicular axes after drawing a free-body diagram.
card.useWhen: an object hangs still, rests on a slope, or slides at constant velocity, and you need to solve for unknown tensions, normal forces, or friction.
card.example: A $4.0\text{ kg}$ lamp ($g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$, $W = 39.2\text{ N}$) hangs at rest from two symmetric ropes each at $30^\circ$ above horizontal → $\sum F_y = 2T\sin 30^\circ - 39.2 = 0$, so $T = 39.2\text{ N}$ in each rope.
card.analogy: A tug-of-war where the ribbon in the middle does not budge: huge forces are pulling both ways, yet they cancel to zero.
